correctness.rationale: Clauwens Theorem 1 gives Adj(Q_T) as Z×V×S(V,T) with S=coker(1-τ), τ(v⊗w)=Tw⊗v. In dimension two, direct 4x4 determinant det(1-τ)=det(1-T)(1-detT) proves S=0 for the stated connected nonresonant locus (and rank defect one at connected detT=1 in odd characteristic). Since T-I invertible, derived subgroup of V⋊_T Z is V and characteristic, and the quotient is Z: any group isomorphism restricts to A∈GL2 and sends the generator to its sign, forcing T similar to U or U^(-1). Nonscalar 2x2 matrices classified by trace/determinant produce (p-2)(p-1) admissible cyclic classes; p-3 admissible scalars add to p²-2p-1. Fixed inversion class would force det=-1,trace=0, contradicting det(1-T)!=0. Inn(Q_T)=V⋊<T> and its translation subgroup characteristic. Direct independent matrix enumeration reproduced p=3,5,7 counts 2,14,34 and F5 T^7=(0,3;1,1), T^24=I. Source verifier has one potentially misleading unmodded det==0 test; independent check used correct mod-p invertibility and separately confirms claim.
